page.layout: One page of text in a single column; numbered thesis lines with centred headings MATHEMATICA and PHYSICA; a catchword "META-" at the lower right. No margin notes. Faint show-through from the reverse side is ignored.

main_text.p: 4. Aliquis poterit dolere tamen causâ doloris non existente.
5. Omnis Generatio Animalium fit mediantibus ovis.
6. Omnibus immobilis & fixus est vitæ terminus.

7. Primorum hominum longævitatis causæ non ex eo petendæ sunt, quòd fuerint primæ mundi origini propiores, aut acuratiorem notitiam τῶν πόων obtinuerint, aut quia cibis crudis & ignis vi non temeratis usi sint, ut credidit Beverovicius Thes. San. c. 3. Sed quia ita liberrimæ Dei sponte erat, & Ecclesiæ necessarium.
8. Omnis vita Corporea in Calido & humido cōsistit, ut & Mors à Calido procedit.
main_text.head: MATHEMATICA.
main_text.p: A Mathematicis demonstratur cujuscunque Trianguli tres Angulos æquivalere tantùm duobus rectis; At dico, fieri posse triangulum, cujus anguli æquivalebunt tribus rectis.
2. Fieri potest aliqua linea quæ propendet ad aliam, & tamen erit Parallela; contra doctrinam Parallelorum quæ vult omnem lineam propendentem seu habentem inclinationem ad aliam non esse Parallelam.
5. Refractio alicujus radij eò magis ad perpendiculum accedit, quò corpus pellucidum solidius est.
main_text.head: PHYSICA.
main_text.p: 2. Nullum Lumen, nullus Calor in sole datur.
Sine demonstratione Mathematica omnes in Physicis cautiunt.

page.notes: The numbers 4 and 2 near the mathematical and physical theses are printed marginal numerals of the numbered series; the unnumbered lines carry printed dots or symbols that are not legible as numbers. The Greek phrase "τῶν πόων" is a faint reading; the second Greek word is uncertain. The catchword "META-" is set at the right foot and is treated as catchword.
